gate.threshold_rule_meaning: The 12th-largest score on the 140 fit-reference prompts. Measured here: 12/140 reference rows clear it, exactly as specified.

fit.render_note: Fitted with --render serving, NOT the `fit` render the shipped kits use. Qwen3.8's chat template injects a 36-token reasoning-effort preamble that the serving path does not reproduce, so a `fit`-render operator is measured in a render the server never produces. Fitting in the serving render removed that confound and did not fix the kit; see known_gaps.
fit.category_quality: AUC 0.9974 in-sample; 100/100 fit positives clear tau; 12/140 reference rows clear it; separation +0.1534 (pos mean +0.1597, neg mean +0.0063).
fit.refusal_quality: sep 1.1239; mu_hm_cos +0.000866 (orthogonalization holds); sd_hm_cos 0.040170; z_harm_mean 13.34; 681/681 harmful and 76/1000 harmless rows reach the 1.50 sigma floor. Fitted on 681 harmful + 1000 harmless rows, which is NOT the 692/554 convention the shipped kits use, so this sigma scale is not comparable to gemma4's or qwen36's.

measured_live.basis: A100 80GB, vLLM 0.32.0, bf16, --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching, serving render (cybergate_mode=baseline, no system prompt, max_tokens=1, temp=0). Every row matched to its decision record by exact prompt sha. 2026-11-02/03.

shipped_category_direction_does_not_tran.RETRACTED_auc_figures: An earlier revision of this file reported AUC 0.5893 against the fit references and 0.5500 against harmless, described as 12 of the kit's own fit positives against 14 of its own fit references. Those prompt lists were typed into a notebook cell rather than read from the corpora: only 3 of the 12 'positives' were in pos_train_cyber_100 and only 6 of the 14 'references' were in neg_ref_14cats_140. Most of the remainder were other-harm prompts, which a working cyber direction is supposed to score LOW -- so that AUC is consistent with the direction working and cannot be used as evidence it does not. Both figures are withdrawn. scripts/fit/score_op_from_dump.py measures this correctly on the full 100 and 140 from the harvest, with the splits read from the replay order file.

what_IS_supported.note: These five are genuine pool-cyber_offense fit positives, keyed by prompt sha, and the live scores and tau are both real, so none of the kit's own highest-scoring fit positives clears its own threshold at serve time. The capture-time scores they were compared against (+0.218 to +0.238) were measured in the FIT render while these are the serving render, so the two columns are not comparable in magnitude -- but the 0-of-5 against tau does not depend on that comparison.

shipped_category_direction_does_not_tran.the_discriminating_evidence: Refitting at the SAME L39 on vLLM's own pooled activations gives 0.9526 held-out recall where the shipped L39 operator fires on none of its own top fit positives. That pair is what establishes the capture geometry as the cause, and neither half of it depends on the retracted AUCs.
shipped_category_direction_does_not_tran.SUPERSEDED_BY: shipped_category_direction_PARTIALLY_transfers, measured on the full corpora. The five-prompt 0-of-5 below is still true but it is five prompts; the full measurement puts the shipped direction at 18% recall on its own 100 positives, so 'fires on none of its top fit positives' was a small-sample artifact of which five were picked.

shipped_refusal_direction_DOES_transfer.note: Clean separation with the 1.50 floor inside a 2.8-z gap. Compressed against the fit -- cos 0.168 live against the 0.537 implied by z_harm_mean 13.34 -- but the z-scale still works because sd_hm is small. mu_hm/sd_hm are still the transformers values and have NOT been re-measured live.

refit_on_vllm_activations.method: 915 prompts replayed at the live server with the activation dump armed, then the same M1 ridge solver and the same R3 threshold rule, fitted on the same 100 positives and 140 references. scripts/fit/harvest_vllm_acts.py then scripts/fit/sweep_layers_from_dump.py.
refit_on_vllm_activations.holdout: cysecbench_val_675, disjoint from the fit corpora, never seen by the fit
refit_on_vllm_activations.note: Refitting at the SAME L39 takes held-out recall from chance to 0.9526: only the capture geometry changed, so the geometry mismatch was the cause and the in-sample 0.9974 was never evidence either way. The in-sample AUC is 0.99+ at all 64 layers INCLUDING those with 0.21 held-out recall, which is why layers are ranked out of sample. L51 and L39 differ by about one standard error -- six prompts of 675 -- so that ordering is not meaningful, and taking the best of 64 biases the winner upward. LEAK IS NOT YET MEASURED on any out-of-sample non-target set, so none of this is yet a gating result.

two_prefills_per_request.note: Every request runs a Pass-1 observation of the user turn and a Pass-2 <think>-injected prefill. publish_decision already dropped Pass-2; the activation dump did not until a620a32, so half of every dump was pooled over server-authored text with nothing in the file to show it.

cross_layer_diagnostic_covers_layers_0_t.note: multi_layer_scores held X0..X43 only. The record is published when the refusal monitor completes at ref_layer=43, so layers above it have not run yet. The dump is unaffected -- it writes per layer straight to disk -- so 44-63 are recoverable offline. Any 'no layer reproduces this' conclusion drawn from the record alone is bounded to 0..ref_layer.

measured_live.provenance: MIXED. The re-fit figures are now RETAINED: qwen38_L55_M1_vllm.json carries its own holdout_recall, leak_splits, in_sample_auc and corpus counts, written by the fit rather than transcribed, and records/harvest_2026-11-02_corpus_digest.json carries the per-split counts and text hashes of the replay. refit_leak_sweep.basis: 3284 prompts replayed at the live server with the dump armed (24 min), then the M1 ridge solver and the R3 rule at every one of the 64 layers. Fitted on 100 positives and 140 references; recall held out on cysecbench_val_675; leak on catqa_test_234, wmdp_bio_test_637, sosbench_bio_498 and 1000 harmless. Positive control passed on all 3284 rows at 1.16e-05.

gemma4_for_comparison.note: measured on a DEPLOYED operator, not offline over harvested activations

refit_leak_sweep.why_not_L51: The sweep ranks by recall minus the worst leak and the two tie exactly at 0.8461, so the ordering between them came from the tie-break on recall. On the three leak sets that metric ignores, L51 is 12x worse into WMDP-bio and 3.5x worse on benign prompts for 3.9 points of recall.
refit_leak_sweep.high_recall_layers_are_the_leaky_ones: L39 leaks 0.2104 into WMDP-bio and L25 leaks 0.2402, at recall 0.9526 and 0.9422. Those directions are substantially generic-harm rather than cyber-specific. The shipped kit chose L39 on in-sample AUC, and L39 is among the least selective layers in the stack -- which an in-sample AUC of 0.9985 could not have revealed.
refit_leak_sweep.NOT_CLEAN_YET: The layer was chosen by looking at recall AND all four leak sets, so every number in this block is optimistically biased by selection over 64 layers. cysecbench_test_675 is still untouched and gives a clean recall. For a clean leak, incorpus_nontarget_leak_378 and pku_cybercrime_612 have not been used for anything. And all of this is offline scoring over harvested activations; gemma4's numbers come from a deployed gate, so the comparison is not yet like for like.

shipped_category_direction_PARTIALLY_tra.basis: The shipped L39 direction scored over the 3284-row vLLM dump with the splits read from the replay order file, at its own tau of +0.06295487. scripts/fit/score_op_from_dump.py, on the full corpora -- not a sampled handful.
shipped_category_direction_PARTIALLY_tra.note: This supersedes two earlier accounts in this file, both of which were too strong. The direction is NOT dead: AUC 0.65 against its own fit references, and the leak at its own threshold is essentially zero -- 0/140 references, 0/1000 harmless, 2/234 CatQA. What failed is the pairing of direction and threshold. The score distribution shrank by about 9x between the two engines (positives at +0.024 against the +0.22 of the capture) while tau stayed where R3 put it on transformers activations, so the threshold now sits above roughly four fifths of the positives. 18% recall at ~0% leak is a working-but-blind gate, not a broken direction.
shipped_category_direction_PARTIALLY_tra.what_this_does_not_settle: How much of the gap a threshold re-derivation alone would close. R3 applied to the SAME 140 references in the vLLM geometry is the same rule in the right space, not a tuned parameter, and scripts/fit/score_op_from_dump.py --retune-tau reports it. At AUC 0.65 the shipped direction cannot reach the re-fit's 0.92 recall at low leak whatever the threshold, so a re-fit is still expected to be needed -- but the decomposition between 'wrong threshold' and 'weaker direction' has not been measured.

known_gaps: THIS KIT AS SHIPPED DOES NOT GATE, and the cause is now MEASURED rather than hypothesised: the category direction was fitted on transformers activations and scores at chance under vLLM (AUC 0.5893 against its own fit references, 0.5500 against harmless), while the refusal direction at L43 transfers cleanly (31/31 harmful over the 1.50 floor, 0/15 harmless). See measured_live. Refitting the category direction on vLLM's own activations at the same L39 gives 0.9526 held-out recall, so the fix is a re-fit in the serving geometry, not a new layer and not a new corpus.

LEAK IS NOT MEASURED for the re-fit. Held-out recall of 0.9615 at L51 is not a gating result on its own -- a direction that fires on everything also scores high recall -- and the only negatives in that run were the 140 the fit used to set tau, whose 11/140 is pinned by the R3 rule rather than measured. CatQA, WMDP-bio, SOSBench-bio and harmless leak are all pending.

SELECTION, not just fitting: the in-sample AUC is 0.99+ at ALL 64 layers, including layers whose held-out recall is 0.21. It ranks nothing and is not evidence of anything. The shipped 0.9974 belongs to this class.

The layer for the re-fit would be chosen on cysecbench_val_675, and taking the best of 64 layers biases that number upward: at n=675 the standard error is 0.0074, so the top ten layers are within noise of each other. cysecbench_test_675 is disjoint from every corpus used here and has deliberately NOT been touched, so one clean measurement remains available.

No canaries. A canary pins a measured verdict so a later run can detect a different checkpoint; with the shipped gate firing on nothing there is no verdict worth pinning. The re-fit must produce them.
NOT measured on any evaluation corpus with a deployed operator. The numbers above are offline scores over harvested activations, not a served kit's recall and leak.

The policy thresholds (revoke_ceil, hysteresis_thresh, in_context_pivot_floor, s_cat_last_pivot_floor) are inherited from Qwen3.6 and were never recalibrated here, so the mid/late veto and rescue paths are untested on this model.
The refusal factor's mu_hm/sd_hm are the transformers-capture values. They work live, but they have not been re-measured on vLLM activations.
bundle_probe_layers is empty, so there is no middle/late candidate consensus for this family.
